source.title: Scaling Up Vision-Language Pretraining for Image Captioning
source.authors: Xiaowei Hu; Zhe Gan; Jianfeng Wang; Zheng-Yuan Yang; Zi-Cheng Liu; Yumao Lu; Li-Juan Wang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines scaling in vision-language pretraining for image captioning, a different setting from language-model pretraining, and reports downstream results across model and data scales.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling results for downstream captioning scores, which bear on V6. Its pretraining metric is masked-token prediction accuracy, not held-out cross-entropy loss; it does not fit loss power laws, test extrapolation from small runs, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Figure values used below are not stated numerically in the text. Comparisons and results cited from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study scales a vision-language captioning model (13M–675M parameters) and its pretraining data (3M–200M pairs). It reports how downstream captioning CIDEr changes with both, which bears on V6 in a new setting. It fits no loss power law and does no extrapolation or compute-optimal analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that scaling pretraining data and model size markedly improves downstream captioning, with larger models benefiting more as data grow. With orders of magnitude more data, model capacity becomes the bottleneck, which motivates training larger models. At 3M pairs, larger models give no significant benefit.
record.recipe_differences: This is an image-captioning vision-language pretraining study using masked-token prediction and downstream captioning metrics, not a language-model held-out-loss scaling-law fit.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect of model size depends on pretraining data scale: larger models show little advantage at 3M examples but a significant advantage above 40M.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretraining masked-token prediction accuracy learning curves for base vs huge models (Fig. 6a). This is accuracy over samples seen, not held-out loss vs scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger vision-language models reach higher masked-token prediction accuracy with fewer pretraining samples.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors describe downstream CIDEr as following a linear-logarithmic trend in model and data size, read from figures only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream captioning CIDEr grows roughly linearly in log model size and log data size when the other factor is not a bottleneck.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is primarily presented in figures, whose values are not numerically transcribed in the text. The study reports downstream captioning metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss and does not fit quantitative predictive scaling laws.

untested.parts: Whether downstream scores can be predicted quantitatively from scale or pretraining loss. No predictor is fitted or validated; the authors only describe a 'linear-logarithmic' trend qualitatively.
Power-law fall of held-out pretraining loss; no loss-vs-scale fit is reported.

Effect of depth/width at a fixed parameter count. Configurations change depth and parameter count together. Table 6 compares encoder vs encoder-decoder and training objectives, not shape at fixed size.
Whether a power-law form holds for pretraining loss in vision-language models; only downstream CIDEr is reported.
Sensitivity of fitted exponents or allocation to fitting choices.

missing.what: Numeric downstream scores across model sizes pretrained on ALT200M. COCO Karpathy CIDEr: base 133.3, large 135.7, huge 139.1. nocaps val overall CIDEr: 106.8, 113.4, 117.3. CC3M dev CIDEr: 111.9, 117.4, 136.8.
nocaps CIDEr for LEMONbase as pretraining data grows. Overall: no pretraining 79.0, CC3M 91.6, CC12M 100.4, ALT200M 106.8.

record.verdict_notes: All model-size and data-size scaling evidence is in figures (Figs 1, 2, 8), except the tables listed under missing. The training objective is sequence-to-sequence masked language modelling, not autoregressive language modelling. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute; the study reports masked-token prediction accuracy and downstream captioning scores instead.
No power-law fits from small runs or tests of predictions on much larger runs.
No fixed-compute optimization or fitted parameter/token allocation trend.
The architecture comparison does not test loss changes from depth, width, or shape at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns image-captioning vision-language pretraining but does not test whether the same power-law form holds for held-out loss in this or other modalities or regimes.
The study reports downstream captioning scores over selected model and data scales, but does not fit or validate a quantitative predictor of downstream performance.
No analysis of power-law exponent or compute-optimal allocation sensitivity to fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Pretraining data of roughly 40M+ pairs; model-size and data-size sweeps; COCO and nocaps CIDEr
relationships.reason: CIDEr rises with both data and model size (r2, r3, r4). Larger models reach base-model scores with 2–8x fewer samples (r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: CIDEr increased with both model and data size, and larger models matched base-model scores using 2–8 times fewer samples.

relationships.reason: At 3M pairs, increasing model size beyond base gives no significant CIDEr gain (r1), so the model-size benefit depends on data scale.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing model size beyond base yields no significant CIDEr improvement with 3M pretraining pairs.
